newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN sees first of oil deal monitors in Iraq Oct 23.
newsitem.headline: UN sees first of oil deal monitors in Iraq Oct 23.

text.p: An advanced team of inspectors from the Dutch firm Saybolt will be sent back to Iraq on October 23 to perform preliminary inspections ahead of possible implementation of the UN-Iraq oil-for-food accord.
Western diplomats said the UN move to redeploy the inspectors was not a signal the oil deal was closer to implementation, but instead was prepartory in nature.

"The secretary-general wants to implement the deal as soon as possible. This deployment is in case that happens sooner. It might not be months and months (before implementation is possible)," the diplomat said.
The UN will deploy three Saybolt inspectors to do the advance work throughout Iraq, the diplomat said.
Saybolt inspectors were pulled out of Iraq in early September when fighting flared in the northern Kurdish regions, resulting in a U.S.-Iraq military confrontation.
The UN has delayed finalizing the oil-for-aid plan due to the renewed fighting in the northern Kurdish regions of Iraq.

The oil-for-food accord would allow $2 billion in oil sales every six months to be used as humanitarian relief for the Iraqi populace suffering under UN-imposed sanction after Iraq invaded Kuwait in 1990.
